Inspired by her work as an America Reads/ 
Counts Tutor at the Boys & Girls Club of Fall 
River, Fall River native Guadalupe Garcia Carrillo 
brought together her passion for design and 
dedication to youth development through 
a community-focused project in AXD 451: 
Community Engagement Design, taught by 
Professor Ziddi Msangi in Fall 2025. 
Motivated by her firsthand experience working 
with students at the Club, she selected the 
Blue Door Club alumni initiative as the focus of 
her self-directed design project. The initiative 
aims to strengthen connections with former 
Club members, increase alumni engagement, 
and support the organization's goal of growing 
Blue Door Club membership from 30 to 100 
members. 
Through her work, she developed a cohesive 
visual identity and a series of promotional 
graphics (page 19) designed to raise awareness 
of the alumni program and encourage former 
members to reconnect with the organization. 
The materials were intentionally created to 
be versatile and accessible. Beyond their 
marketing purpose, several of the designs 
were repurposed by current Boys & Girls 
Club students as coloring pages, creating an 
unexpected opportunity for youth engagement 
and creativity. 
The project reflected the student's dual role as 
both a tutor and designer. By combining service, 
creativity, and community engagement, this 
project helped support the Boys & Girls Club of 
Fall River's mission while demonstrating how 
student talents can create meaningful impact 
beyond the classroom.
